LESSON: THE ATOM

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: CHEMISTRY
Strand: Inorganic chemistry
Topic 1.2: The Atom
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 24

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers The Atom under Inorganic chemistry. It is aligned with the Kenya Institute of Curriculum Development (KICD) CBC design.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on The Atom together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Communication and Collaboration: as the learner listens keenly and actively using open questions while discussing

with peers the relationship between atomic number, mass number and number of electrons in atoms of elements.

● Digital literacy: as the learner continuously learns to use digital platforms while watching animations on atomic

models, isotopes and electron arrangement of atoms.

● Creativity and Imagination: as the learner experiments with ideas while modelling the structure of s and p orbitals

using locally available materials.

Learning to learn: as the learner reflects on their own work as they practise illustration of electron arrangements for

the first 20 elements using s and p orbitals.

Values:
● Social justice: as the learner advocates for harmonious relationship in groups while discussing the meaning of

isotopes and relative atomic mass

Integrity: as the learner shows self-discipline by appropriately using digital devices to watch animations, simulations

or videos on electron arrangement of the atom

10

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs)

● Socio-Economic and Environmental issues (Environmental conservation): as the learner responsibly uses locally

available materials to model the structure of s and p orbitals.

● Life skills (Self-esteem): as the learner gains confidence while presenting findings on the meaning of isotopes

and relative atomic mass.

● Socio-Economic and Environmental issues (global citizenship): as the learner brainstorms with peers on the

contributions of scientists in the development of atomic theory/models.

Suggested learning resources:

Adapted digital resources (adapted computers with larger screens and text creation software), improvised resources

from the environment, stationary (manilla papers and marker pens), adapted writing resources (heavy-gauge paper and

page turners), positioning devices (chest and neck braces), print and non-print media (animation on electron

arrangement in s and p orbitals).
